paper: RegTrack: Uncovering Global Disparities in Third-party Advertising and Tracking
authors: Tanya Prasad, Rut Vora, Soo Yee Lim, Nguyen Phong Hoang, Thomas Pasquier (University of British Columbia)
venue: NDSS Workshop on Measurements, Attacks, and Defenses for the Web (MADWeb) 2026
pageNumbers: Pages refer to the NDSS PDF above (title page = page 1).
terms: A&T = advertising and tracking third-party domains.
rules: The paper tested only two consent states: no click and accept-all. It did NOT test rejecting. Never say 'rejecting removes X trackers'.
These are averages from a crawl of 743 sites, not measurements of the site you are on.

facts.text: RegTrack crawled 743 websites from 8 locations, with 4 browsers and 2 cookie-consent states.
From Ohio, clicking accept-all raised the average number of advertising and tracking domains per site from 48.5 to 56.2, about 16% more.
From France, clicking accept-all raised the average number of advertising and tracking domains per site from 9.3 to 33.9, about 265% more.
Before any click, sites without a cookie banner loaded 37 to 58 advertising and tracking domains for visitors outside the EU, versus 8 to 10 for EU visitors.
In Ohio, the Brave browser saw 31% fewer advertising and tracking domains than Chrome.
Half of the sites accounted for 97% of the advertising and tracking domains observed.
For U.S. visitors (Ohio and California), about 69% to 72% of tracking requests went to servers in the same region.
The authors note they modeled only two consent states (no click and accept-all).
